_note: Frozen content for design review. One automation per page, each with the tactic and the time it actually returns.
brief: Five automations that give back ten hours a week

slots.note: Five automations, each one built in an afternoon. None of them touch the actual work.

slots.title: Sorting
slots.body: Reading every message as it lands is not diligence, it is interruption. Most email is not for now, it is for later, and almost none of it needs a decision on arrival.
slots.tacticText: Route by sender and keyword, then read the low-priority pile once a day.

slots.title: Booking
slots.body: Five messages to agree one half-hour call is the most expensive thing on any calendar, and it happens every single week without anyone noticing the cost.
slots.tacticText: Send one link with your real availability instead of proposing times.

slots.title: Capture
slots.body: Every task and decision rebuilt from memory is a small tax you pay twice. Once when you forget it, and again when you reconstruct it badly.
slots.tacticText: Template the projects you repeat so setup stops being a decision.

slots.title: Billing
slots.body: Chasing money is the least enjoyable hour of the month and the one most likely to be postponed, which is exactly why it should not require a person.
slots.tacticText: Put deposits, reminders and receipts on a schedule and never mention them.

slots.title: Recaps
slots.body: Writing the same weekly summary from scratch is a habit inherited from a job nobody has any more. The data already exists somewhere and it does not need retyping.
slots.tacticText: Pull one page automatically and spend the time reading it instead.

slots.title: Upkeep
slots.body: Automations rot quietly. A rule that silently stops firing costs more than the manual work it replaced, because you have stopped checking.
slots.tacticText: Review every rule once a quarter and delete the ones you cannot explain.

slots.headline: Ten hours
slots.body: The point was never efficiency. It was getting back the part of the week where the actual work happens, and none of this touches that part.
